track: C (AeroTrack temporal / tracking / prediction system; experiments/aerotrack_temporal) -- separate from Track A (Anti-UAV reproduction) and Track B (AeroTrack detector)
registered: see the git commit that added this file (2026-10-05): after TRAIN-only tuning of the classical forecasters and TRAIN/dev smoke tests of the learned ones, before ANY forecaster (classical or learned) is evaluated on VAL in this experiment
class: controlled experiment; fitting on TRAIN, recipe/architecture choices on a TRAIN-held-out dev split, ONE registered pass on VAL; TEST sealed (tc_data refuses it outside a final evaluation)
question: For image-plane UAV trajectories (Anti-UAV IR, Anti-UAV RGB, CST complete release), does a learned forecaster beat strong classical forecasters, is its uncertainty better calibrated, and does the absolute image position (camera re-centring) carry forecastable information?
prior_evidence: experiments/systems/reports/forecast_gen_temporal_fp_g4_full_e20_data_unified.md (VAL, tracker histories, symmetric-window detector): on Anti-UAV IR the Kalman forecast is no better than zero velocity (ADE 28.0 vs 27.8 px) and its 95 % ellipses cover 0.73 (0.35-0.44 on sudden jumps)

TRAIN-only probe (results/runs/aerotrack_temporal/c1/classical_tuning_probe0_pooled.json): pooled over domains, constant position (56.0 px) beats damped velocity (60.0), Kalman (60.0), constant velocity (104.9) and constant acceleration (625); the tuned damping / velocity noise sat on the grid edges, so the grids were widened and a mean-reversion (gimbal re-centring) baseline added before this registration

data.builder: experiments/aerotrack_temporal/scripts/tc_data.py (official annotations; CST from data/cst_anti_uav_full = the complete release; per-sequence label sha256 in results/runs/aerotrack_temporal/_data/traj_<split>.json)
data.train: TRAIN groups with md5(group) % 10 != 0 (group = Anti-UAV recording session with IR and RGB together, or CST sequence)
data.dev: TRAIN groups with md5(group) % 10 == 0: learned models' epoch choice and the architecture choice only
data.val: official VAL: Anti-UAV 67 IR + 67 RGB sequences, CST 40 sequences; read only by tc_c1.py --stage val

samples: anchor t: target visible at t and t-1 in the history source and visible at >= 1 of t+1..t+24; history L = 16 frames (t-15..t, causal, unit-tested), horizon H = 24 frames; every eligible anchor (stride 1); errors only on visible future frames; pixel units of each sequence's native frame

conditions.C1a (this registration): oracle histories: the ground-truth trajectory up to t
conditions.C1b (registered separately, later): tracker histories: STE outputs on VAL detection caches of a CAUSAL detector (corpus-v2 stock or causal-window run), so that no history value depends on frames after t

classical.tuning: per domain on TRAIN: parameters of dcv / ou / oudcv / kalman by pooled TRAIN ADE over the grids in tc_c1.py; the Kalman covariance scale by TRAIN NLL (scaling Q and R together leaves the mean unchanged); a chosen value on a grid edge is flagged in classical_tuning.json
classical.reference: per domain, the classical forecaster with the lowest TRAIN ADE (recorded in results/runs/aerotrack_temporal/c1/classical_tuning.json before --stage val)

families.tfm: 2-layer pre-norm transformer, d 64, 4 heads, anchor token pooled

learned.inputs: per history frame: visible flag, displacement to c_t, log size ratio (zeros when invisible), in percent of the image width; global: log target size; abs variant adds the anchor position in the image (c_t / (W, H) - 0.5)
learned.outputs: per horizon h = 1..24: mean displacement and log sigma per axis (diagonal Gaussian)
learned.recipe: Gaussian NLL on visible future points; AdamW lr 2e-3, wd 1e-4, batch 1024, 12 epochs, linear warm-up 5 % then cosine; gradient clip 5; the epoch with the lowest dev NLL is kept; CPU, deterministic seeds
learned.training_pool: one model for all three domains (no domain input)

arms.main: mlp / gru / tfm with abs inputs, clean histories, 3 seeds each
arms.architecture_choice: the family with the lowest seed-mean dev NLL = the C1 model (decided before --stage val)
arms.noabs: the C1 model's family without the absolute-position input, 3 seeds
arms.aug: the C1 model's family trained on augmented histories (Gaussian jitter sigma = 0.1 x target size on every visible history centre, dropout p 0.1 of frames before t-1), 3 seeds; a-priori noise model, no VAL statistics

metrics.primary: per domain pooled ADE (px) over h = 1..24 and visible future frames
metrics.probabilistic: per domain mean Gaussian NLL (nats per 2-D point, pixel units); coverage of the 50 / 68 / 90 / 95 % ellipses; calibration error = mean |coverage - p| over p = 0.1..0.9
metrics.secondary: FDE@24, error by horizon (1, 2, 4, 8, 12, 16, 24), median error, error / target size, miss rates (> 2 x target size, > 20 px)
metrics.inference: paired cluster bootstrap over VAL sequences (B = 2000, seed 0) of the pooled-ADE difference and of the NLL difference, per domain

H1_point.comparison: C1 model (abs, clean) vs the domain's classical reference, each seed separately
H1_point.SUPPORTED: in that domain, for all 3 seeds: relative ADE change <= -5 % and bootstrap CI upper bound < 0
H1_point.LOSES: for all 3 seeds: bootstrap CI lower bound > 0 (the learned forecaster is worse -- a reportable result)

H2_uncertainty.comparison: C1 model vs the TRAIN-calibrated Kalman, each seed
H2_uncertainty.SUPPORTED: for all 3 seeds: NLL lower with bootstrap CI upper bound < 0 AND calibration error lower than the Kalman's
H2_uncertainty.LOSES: for all 3 seeds: Kalman NLL lower with CI excluding 0

H3_absolute_position.comparison: C1 model family abs vs noabs, seed i vs seed i
H3_absolute_position.a_priori_direction: improvement on Anti-UAV (gimbal-following footage); no directional expectation on CST
H3_absolute_position.SUPPORTED: for all 3 seed pairs: relative ADE change <= -2 % and CI upper bound < 0
H3_absolute_position.REVERSED: for all 3 seed pairs: CI lower bound > 0

hypotheses.H4_augmentation: descriptive only on oracle histories; decided in C1b on tracker histories

multiplicity: 3 domains x 3 hypotheses; each claim requires all three seeds; no pooled-over-domain claims; every arm and domain is reported whatever its outcome
adoption_rule: the system adopts the C1 model as its forecaster only in domains where H1 is SUPPORTED and H2 is not LOSES; elsewhere it keeps the domain's classical reference (with the TRAIN-calibrated Kalman covariance if the reference has none). A learned forecaster that does not beat the classical one is not adopted.

component_gate.measured_failure: CV / Kalman forecasts are worse than constant position on gimbal footage and their 95 % ellipses under-cover (prior evidence above)
component_gate.why: image-plane motion = target motion + camera re-centring + re-slews; inertial models assume the first only
component_gate.baseline: per-domain TRAIN-tuned best of ten classical forecasters, incl. mean reversion to the image centre (ou, oudcv) and a calibrated Kalman
component_gate.novelty: modest: learned trajectory forecasters are standard; the measurable contribution is gimbal-aware, calibrated forecasting for tiny UAVs inside a deployable stack, which must beat a physics prior (ou) that encodes the same effect
component_gate.cost: < 0.5 M parameters; microseconds per target on CPU; minutes of CPU training
component_gate.isolating_ablation: abs vs noabs (H3); learned vs ou / oudcv (inside H1's reference set)
component_gate.exportable: MLP / GRU / transformer export to ONNX opset 18 (checked before adoption)
component_gate.falsifier: H1 NOT_SUPPORTED or LOSES in every domain

run_order: tc_c1.py --stage train --variants abs (mlp / gru / tfm x 3 seeds), architecture choice on dev, then --variants noabs,aug for the chosen family
commit classical_tuning.json + learned_registry.json (checkpoint sha256) -> tc_c1.py --stage val (one pass) -> reports/C1_trajectory_forecasting.{json,md}
compute: CPU only (the GPU stays with the queued GPU campaigns)

amendments.when: 2026-10-05, after the first per-domain TRAIN tuning and before any VAL access
amendments.what: classical grids widened: look-back k adds 12 and 15 (15 = the whole 16-frame history; mv15 added), oudcv damping adds 0.98 / 1.0 and k 8 / 15, Kalman q_pos adds 1/160 / 1/80, covariance scale range 0.01-500 (was 0.05-20); natural limits (k 1 / 15, g 0 / 1, rho 1) are no longer flagged as edges
amendments.why: on CST the TRAIN optimum sat on artificial edges (dcv k = 8, Kalman q_pos = 1/40, covariance scale = 20 = grid maximum), i.e. the classical references (and the Kalman calibration baseline for H2) would have been under-tuned; the anti-UAV optimum of the CV Kalman is its constant-position limit (q_pos max, q_vel and r_meas min), reported as such
